references.text: Previously, a dispute also arose among the disciples about which of them was the greatest. [ref:Luk 9:46|Luke 9:46] shows that this was a recurring theme among the disciples.
Jesus' immediate response to the dispute: He contrasts worldly dominion with servant leadership. [ref:Luk 22:25-27|Luke 22:25-27] is the direct exhortation that follows the dispute in verse 24.
In [ref:Mark 9:33-34|Mark 9:33-34], the disciples discussed among themselves about which of them was the greatest, a parallel theme to the dispute during the last meal.

Jesus teaches the disciples that whoever wants to be great among them must be their servant. [ref:Mark 10:42-45|Mark 10:42-45] gives Jesus' teaching on servant leadership as a direct response to the dispute over rank.
The disciples ask Jesus who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven, and Jesus answers by pointing to a child as an example of humility. [ref:Matt 18:1-4|Matthew 18:1-4] shows the same issue.

James and John's mother asks for places of honor for her sons, which leads to anger among the other disciples. [ref:Matt 20:20-28|Matthew 20:20-28] illustrates the disciples' struggle for precedence and Jesus' teaching on service.

Jesus teaches that the greatest among you must be your servant, and whoever exalts themselves will be humbled. [ref:Matt 23:11-12|Matthew 23:11-12] expresses the principle that greatness involves service.

Paul exhorts humility after Christ's example, who did not cling to equality with God but emptied himself and took the form of a servant. [ref:Fil 2:3-8|Philippians 2:3-8] stands in strong contrast to the disciples' dispute over who was greatest.
[ref:Rom 12:10|Romans 12:10] exhorts believers to outdo one another in showing honor, an attitude that counters the dispute over rank that the disciples had.

[ref:1 Pet 5:5|1 Peter 5:5] encourages putting on humility toward one another, for God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. This is the opposite attitude of the disciples' dispute over greatness.
[ref:Ordsp 13:10|Proverbs 13:10] says that pride only leads to strife. The disciples' quarrel about who was greatest is an example of how pride creates conflict.
